explain.say: Muscles run on a chemical called ATP. In a sprint they use their fastest backup stores within seconds, and the chemical waste from rapid energy use, phosphate and acid, interferes with the grabbing filaments inside the fibres.

faq.q: Does lactic acid make muscles tired?
faq.a: Not mainly. Muscles do make lactate in hard exercise, but it is reused as fuel. Tiredness comes from several things together, including phosphate and acid build-up, falling fuel stores and the brain reducing its drive.
asks: Is lactic acid the cause of muscle burn?

faq.a: When muscles break down ATP and their fast backup fuel quickly, phosphate and hydrogen ions build up inside the fibres. These make it harder for calcium to switch on contraction and for myosin to pull.
asks: Tell me about waste building up

faq.a: Glycogen is a store of sugar, made of many glucose units linked together, kept in muscles and the liver. During long exercise muscles use it up, and when it runs low they tire.
asks: Tell me about the sugar store emptying

faq.q: Why do muscles feel sore a day or two later?
faq.a: Delayed soreness comes from tiny strains in muscle fibres, especially after unfamiliar exercise, and the repair work that follows. It is not caused by lactic acid, which clears within an hour or so.
asks: Why am I sore the day after exercise?

faq.q: How does the brain affect muscle tiredness?
faq.a: Scientists find that the brain reduces the signals it sends to working muscles during long or hard effort, which may help protect the body. This is called central fatigue.

facts: Muscles use ATP for contraction and store only enough for a few seconds of hard work.
Lactate produced during exercise is used as a fuel by the heart and other muscles.
